title: Helmsman release orchestrator: policy compiler for fine-grained traffic manifests
creator: Ariana Patel
description: Design and implement the Helmsman policy compiler: a deterministic translator that converts high-level rollout blueprints (traffic weights, step schedules, guardrails, shadowing rules, and A/B experiment knobs) into runtime-validated traffic manifests for the serving runtime. The compiler must support expressive constructs (percentile-based SI thresholds, error-budget-aware holds, conditional step escalation, shadow sampling rates) while producing compact, auditable manifests that the routing layer can enforce atomically. This work includes a validation engine, a simulation harness for preflight checks, a compact JSON manifest schema, and Console bindings for edit/preview/visualization.
acceptance_criteria: Helmsman accepts declarative rollout blueprints and outputs a runtime manifest conforming to the new policy schema
Manifests include per-step traffic split, timeout/latency guards (p50/p95 rules), error-rate thresholds, and automatic rollback predicates
Preflight simulation produces a summary CSV and deterministic outcome for a chosen workload trace
Console UI shows a step timeline preview and allows edit -> compile -> dry-run without applying changes
End-to-end test covers shadow traffic routing and A/B weight convergence in integration environment
Performance: compiler completes typical blueprint (5 steps, 3 variants) in <150ms in CI run
implementation_notes: Create a small, language-agnostic DSL for conditional steps; compile to manifest v2 (compact JSON)
Validator should surface human-friendly errors and line numbers linking to Console editor
Integrate simulation harness with existing trace-replayer used by ENG-99785
Expose compile API as a separate service behind an authz boundary for Private customers
Add schema versioning and migration strategy for runtime to support gradual rollout

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Overly expressive DSL could lead to unsafe rollouts. Mitigation: whitelist runtime-safe operators and require opt-in for experimental predicates.
Risk: Customer manifests diverging between private and hosted. Mitigation: compile API parity tests and cross-environment schema compatibility checks.
Risk: Auto-rollback oscillation under noisy metrics. Mitigation: require hysteresis window and error-budget smoothing; add canary cooldown step.
test_plan: Unit tests for compiler transforms (100% coverage for core transforms)
Property tests for compositional behavior of step conditions
Integration tests: deployment pipeline -> compile -> apply to canary cluster -> observe metrics for 30m
Chaos tests: simulate node preemption and verify escrow/rollback behavior
Regression tests: ensure existing runtime rollouts (legacy schema) still accepted until migration completes
